gaps.hint: you ___ a match, but ___ the other team
gaps.explanation: 'Win' takes the game or prize as object (win a match); 'beat/defeat' take the opponent as object.

gaps.sentence: He ___ her on her presentation and her handling of questions.
We ___ all major credit cards at the box office.
gaps.explanation: 'Accept' means to take or agree to something offered; 'except' means not including.

gaps.sentence: She has lived in this street ___ 2015.
gaps.hint: starting point of a period up to now
gaps.explanation: 'Since' is used with a point in time when the situation started and continues; 'for' is used with a length of time.

gaps.sentence: It's hard to choose ___ the two options.
gaps.explanation: 'Between' is used for two people or things; 'among' for a group of more than two.

gaps.hint: past participle after 'have'; the verb takes no object
gaps.explanation: 'Rise' (rise, rose, risen) takes no object: sales have risen. 'Raise' takes an object: they raised prices.

gaps.sentence: Be careful not to ___ your passport at the check-in desk.
gaps.explanation: 'Lose' is the verb; 'loose' means not tight.

gaps.sentence: The committee will ___ your application at its May meeting.
gaps.explanation: The finite verb slot needs 'consider'; 'considerable' means large.
